subject: Post-demo: ops handshake required for multi-tenant SLA and isolation rubric
messages:
From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.com>
To: Anna Lee <anna.lee@clarityhealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-04-11T09:18:00-07:00
Subject: Post-demo: ops handshake required for multi-tenant SLA and isolation rubric

Hi Anna — thanks again for taking the demo this morning. Wanted to capture the call recap and the small ops "handshake" we discussed so your security and infra teams can quickly validate a path forward.

TL;DR: ClarityHealth is leaning Hosted API for initial integration but needs assurance around noisy-neighbor impact on 99th-percentile latency and an ops-runbook for graceful fallback (to Dedicated) if we hit sustained SLAs. You asked for a short checklist + examples of isolation boundaries and SLO-driven rollout playbooks. Attached: redwood-ops-handshake-checklist.pdf and isolation-rubric-v1.xlsx.

Key notes from the call:
- Primary use: near-real-time patient-facing chat (avg request ~750 tokens, bursty mornings 9–11am PT).
- SLO target: p95 < 200ms, p99 < 800ms for text-generation endpoints.
- Regulatory: PHI in prompts is a possibility, but for now they plan token-scrubbing on client side; may require Private later.
- Concern: "noisy neighbor" during peak windows; want concrete mitigations and triggers for Dedicated failover.

Requested artifacts (what you said you need):
1) Short operations checklist for Hosted that enumerates monitoring signals, thresholds, and automatic fallback triggers.
2) Example isolation boundary diagram (what Dedicated buys you vs hosted) and estimated RTO for failover.
3) Confirmation of metrics we can expose to customers (token-level latency, model-level tail latencies, capacity headroom).

Proposed next steps (I can own):
- Internal: Marissa to produce a one-page ops rubric + proposed failover triggers (by Tue 4/14).
- Technical: Karthik to run a short capacity-sensitivity test with a synthetic burst profile (we'll share results).
- Customer: 30-min technical ops call with your infra lead to walk through the rubric and confirm thresholds (schedule week of 4/20).

Would you like us to include a short POC estimate for Reserved/Dedicated capacity as an explicit fallback option? If so we can attach rough monthly cost and capacity sizing.

Thanks — Sergio
Sergio Alvarez
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
sergio@redwood.com

Attachments:
- redwood-ops-handshake-checklist.pdf (1 page)
- isolation-rubric-v1.xlsx (3 tabs: metrics, triggers, responsibilities)

From: Anna Lee <anna.lee@clarityhealth.com>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.com>
Cc: ops@clarityhealth.com
Date: 2026-04-11T10:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: ops handshake required for multi-tenant SLA and isolation rubric

Hi Sergio — thanks for the clear recap and for the attachments. This is exactly what our infra team needs to validate the initial path. A couple quick clarifications: 

1) The p99 target you listed aligns with our internal SLA goal for the patient chat. Anything above ~1s at the p99 is a blocker for go-live.
2) We will not send PHI in production for the first 90 days, but the architecture must support an easy migration to Private/VPC later.
3) For failover: we want an automated alert + suggested human-in-the-loop decision (ops engineer) before spinning up Dedicated — we have cost constraints and want to avoid false positives.

Please proceed with the rubric and a short POC estimate for Dedicated as a planned fallback. Also, can Redwood share an example of the metrics dashboard (token-level latency + headroom) you expose? A screenshot or short recording would be helpful.

Best,
Anna
Anna Lee
Director of Product Operations | ClarityHealth
anna.lee@clarityhealth.com

Forwarded attachments: none

From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-04-11T11:20:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Post-demo: ops handshake required for multi-tenant SLA and isolation rubric — action items

Marissa / Karthik — forwarding Anna's confirmation (above). Two immediate asks:

Marissa: please produce the 1-page ops rubric that specifically calls out the alert thresholds we want to propose (suggested list below). Keep it customer-facing and avoid deep infra detail. Deliverable due: 2026-04-14 EOD.

Karthik: please run a short synthetic p99 sensitivity test for the chat model with the following profile:
- Baseline steady-state: 50 concurrent sessions, avg 750 tokens
- Burst profile: 300 concurrent sessions for 15 minutes
- Measure: p95, p99 latency and KV cache hit-rate impacts.
- Note: include CPU/GPU utilization and any queue growth metrics.

Suggested alert thresholds (first pass):
- p95 latency > 250ms for 5m -> notify on-call + increase autoscale priority
- p99 latency > 800ms for 2m -> send high-severity alert and raise capacity headroom flag
- Sustained p99 > 1s for 5m -> recommend ops call and consider Dedicated reservation plan

Also, Anna asked for a screenshot of the Redwood token-level latency dashboard — I can share a link to a demo recording. Can you prepare a 2-slide mock of the dashboard to send to them?

Thanks — Sergio

Attachments referenced: redwood-ops-handshake-checklist.pdf

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-04-13T15:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Post-demo: ops handshake required for multi-tenant SLA and isolation rubric — action items

Thanks — compiling draft materials now. Deliverables and owners: 

1) Ops handshake one-pager (customer-facing) — Marissa (draft attached). Highlights: monitoring signals, explicit failover decision tree (human-in-loop gate), runbook for incident remediation, and recommended verification tests.
2) Dedicated fallback estimate (ballpark monthly & lead time) — Sergio to draft pricing note; I'll sanity-check.
3) Tech deliverable: Karthik to run stress test and produce p95/p99 baseline + burst report by 4/16. Karthik will also attach a 2-slide mock dashboard for Anna.

Notes on decision tree we propose to show ClarityHealth:
- Tier 1: transient tail spikes (<2 minutes) -> autoscale/evict prefetched work, no ops page.
- Tier 2: recurring p99 spikes (2–10 minutes) -> automated throttling of non-critical routes, notify ops, prepare dedicated capacity window.
- Tier 3: sustained p99 >1s for >5 minutes -> trigger ops playbook and propose Dedicated reservation for peak windows (includes expected capacity and cost bucket).

I'm attaching a one-page draft (redwood-ops-handshake-checklist.pdf). Please review and I'll finalize for Anna.

Marissa Cole
Principal Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com

Attachments:
- redwood-ops-handshake-checklist.pdf (draft v0.2)
